findings.finding: Use f(n)=((n‑1)(s‑1))/s where s=smallest odd prime divisor of n‑1. For c≠4M, s=3 if c≡1(mod3) else smallest odd prime of c. For c=0, s=5. For c=4M, s=11549 (found by testing 5·3^2025!≡1 mod p). Compute S=10−(1/5+5/11549+1/11+1/5081287+1/29+1/17)−2/2025!. Write S=(N0·K−2D)/(DK) with K=2025!, D=5·11549·11·5081287·29·17, N0=10D−A_num. Reduce fraction (gcd=54230). p+q mod 99991 = 18016.

Key: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)=n·min_{S|n}g(S)/S, where g(S)=min lcm for sum S. Global min ratio=6/11 (S multiple 11). For N=M+small c, divisors are primes of c+1 (≠3). Compute min g(S)/S among those S≥6. Results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum=125561848/19033825 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991=8687. Pitfalls: ignore 3‑factor, ensure S≥6, use reduced fractions; 2025!·ratio integer.

f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c)=min c with a|c,b|c, a+b+c=n ⇒ n=c·(1+1/d1+1/d2). Let D=g·u·v+u+v (d1=g·u,d2=g·v). α=g·u·v/D. D|n ⇔ c≡−1 (mod t) & c≡0 (mod 3^e) (t coprime to 3). For M=3^{2025!}, M≡1 (mod t),0 (mod 3^e). Compute smallest D (by α) dividing each n_i. Results: α:2/3,2/3,16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167. Sum=224414944/57101475 ⇒ p+q≡41754 (mod 99991).

Use f(n)=n·min_{s|n}(LCM_min(s)/s). Base ratios: 11→6/11,7→4/7,10→3/5,13→8/13,9→2/3,… Compute n=M+c (M=3^{2025!}). M≡1 mod p≤2025 (p≠3). Find smallest s|n among {11,7,10,13,9,…}. For each c get r: c=0→9|M ⇒r=2/3; c=4M→s=??; etc. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·r⌋/2025!. Sum →p/q, compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfall: assume divisor 1 triple; need minimal LCM triple.

f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c)=L where a+b+c=n, a,b|L.  Use d1,d2>1 with L+L/d1+L/d2=n ⇒L=n·(g·u·v)/(g·u·v+u+v).  D=g·u·v+u+v must divide n.  Smallest D gives α=numer/D.  Compute for n=M,5M,M+c_i (c_i small).  D=9→α=2/3; D=25→16/25; D=47→30/47; D=97→64/97; D=167→110/167.  Sum=224414944/57101475 →p+q≡41754 (mod 99991).

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)=n·min_{S|n}g(S)/S, where g(S)=min lcm for sum S. Global min ratio=6/11 (S multiple 11). For N=M+ c, N’s small divisors are primes of c+1 (≠3). Compute min g(S)/S from those: c=0,4M ⇒2/3; c=1848374⇒16/25; c=10162574⇒30/47; c=265710644⇒64/97; c=44636594⇒110/167. Sum=125561848/19033825 ⇒(p+q) mod 99991=8687. Pitfall: ignore 3‑factor, ensure denominators divide 2025!.

f(n)=min pq/(pq+p+q) with t=pq+p+q|n (a,b=n/t·q,c=n/t·p). Minimal ratios: 6/11 (t=11),4/7(t=14),10/17(t=17),3/5(t=20)… For n=M=3^N, M≡1(mod 11,14,…), M≡0(mod 9,27). ⇒f(M)=2/3·M, f(5M)=2/3·5M. For n=M+small c, test t≤4000 (p,q≤60). Found ratios: 34/53,30/47,75/103,110/167. Sum S=2/3+10/3+34/53+30/47+75/103+110/167=285650357/42847691. (p+q) mod 99991=27613. Pitfalls: ensure M mod t via CRT (3‑power part 0, coprime part 1). Use floor term negligible for small c.
